thread.title: Apple Shows This Leadership Trait, Dow Jones Leads; 2 Sectors Reverse

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Apple Shows This Leadership Trait, Dow Jones Leads; 2 Sectors Reverse
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) continued to show market leadership. The megacap tech refused to give up any of its solid gains over the prior three sessions while Microsoft ( MSFT ) edged higher for a fourth day in a row as large and megacaps outperformed the small-cap space in stocks today.
X While the Dow Jones industrial average gained nearly 0.6% for its fourth win in a row. The Russell 2000 dived 0.5%. But the latter has a bigger year-to-date return. The Russell, at 1694, boasts a 10.3% advance. The Dow, at 24,919, is up just 0.8%.
Fellow Dow Jones component Microsoft ( MSFT ) edged up less than 0.2% to 102.01 but is now within spitting distance of hitting new highs. The diversified software and consumer electronics powerhouse has advanced 18% since breaking out of a six-week flat base at 86.30 in heavy volume on Dec. 15.
The S&P 500 rose 0.3%. NYSE volume edged slightly higher, according to early data. Defensive sectors including food and utilities, as well as cyclical groups such as semiconductors, homebuilders, steel and automakers, paced the advance. Roughly eight of IBD's 197 industry groups rose 1% or more. (See the entire list of 197 IBD industries and the six-month relative strength rankings here.)
The banking and transport sectors fell, losing some of their recent big gains. The Dow transports fell just 0.3%, but IBD's truck transport industry group skidded 1.7% lower. JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) halted a three-day win streak, losing 0.6% to 106.62 and failing to close back above its 200-day line.
Techs And Consumer Leaders Still Shine As noted in a prior Stock Market Today column , Apple cleared the 5% buy zone from a 179.04 correct entry in a narrow double bottom.
Apple, rising to as high as 191.28 on Wednesday before closing off just 0.1% at 190.35, is now up 6.3% past the proper buy point . It's now extended.
Micron Technology ( MU ), a current member of IBD's Sector Leaders, outperformed the market with a 3% gain to 55.74 in light trade. The data storage play reclaimed its 50-day moving average for the first time in two weeks and is trying to mold a new base.
Stitch Fix ( SFIX ), a curated-apparel service popular among the young, surged to new highs with a 6% lift to 32.99. The Nasdaq stock is now up more than 9% past a cup-without-handle entry point of 30.17.
Volume zoomed to triple its usual level of 2.1 million shares per day. The stock did suffer a sell signal after falling more than 8% from the entry, yet has recovered.
San Francisco-based Stitch Fix notched $977 million in revenue in 2017, up 34%. This year, the Street sees the top line bulging 26% to $1.23 billion, then rising another 20% to $1.47 billion in 2019. However, earnings are seen slipping 41% to 19 cents a share in 2018 and falling another 26% to 14 cents a share in 2019 as the company invests aggressively to expand its services.
The company shows excellent operating cash flow, coming in at $1.38 a share in 2017. That's quadruple the 32 cents it earned that year.
Whipsawing In Energy Names Energy stocks were active, but a relatively large group of the sector's leaders retreated from session highs.
Cactus ( WHD ), featured in IPO Leaders in the past and the new IBD Stock of the Day , bounced within a wide range of nearly 4 points before ending the day down more than 5% to 33.69. Volume surged five times above its 50-day average.
For three sessions in a row, the stock tried to clear a 35.28 buy point in a narrow cup with handle . But some funds have used the opportunity to dump shares. Cactus went public at 19 a share on Feb. 8.
A good cup with handle typically shows a minimum length of seven weeks. Think of it this way: The left side of the cup may form over three weeks, the right side in three weeks, and a downward-sloping handle over one week. That all adds up to seven weeks.
However, IBD research has found that in some rare cases, a stock with extraordinary fundamentals can bolt out of a six-week cup with handle so long as it shows excellent price-volume action, has glowing fundamentals, owns a leadership spot in its industry, and is rising along a confirmed market uptrend.
In his 2004 classic, "The Successful Investor," IBD founder Bill O'Neil wrote that the cup with handle "should be at least six to eight weeks in length, starting with the first week closing down off the stock's top."
On the positive side, the expert in wellheads and oil rig-related gear found buying support near its 50-day moving average. Cactus has rallied as much 97% from its IPO price.
Notice how sell-offs in early and mid-June sent the stock briefly below the 50-day moving average.
The Emerging Markets Struggle The iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) ETF cooled off after rising sharply the past few weeks. The popular exchange-traded fund edged 0.4% lower to 43.97 in quiet trade. EEM is down nearly 7% year to date, hurt in large part by its 32% weighting in China.
Notice how EEM posted a key sell signal on Feb. 5 as the ETF sliced through the 50-day moving average in huge volume. EEM eventually tested institutional buying support at the long-term 200-day moving average, bounced sharply and briefly flung above the 50-day line, and tried to build a new base.
Yet since March, EEM has continued to struggle as the 50-day line became a level of resistance. The 50-day moving average has also been sliding for more than three months, indicating a negative intermediate-term trend.
Lewis Alexander, chief economist at Nomura Securities, noted in a new monthly global economic outlook that his team believes "global growth has peaked and, as it slows, we are most cautious in EM (emerging markets)."
"We are specifically forecasting that global growth will slow from an annual rate of 4.0% in 2018 to 3.7% in 2019," he added.
